1.name: Solid perception
1.question: Whose world is this?
1.gloss: all images revolve around a central and privileged image
1.difference: One body owns the frame: either we see through its eyes (POV, eyelid/mask/windscreen framing) or we see it held at the hub with everything else arranged around it — and the image would lose its organising centre if that body were removed.

flips.if: It is Liquid instead if the camera keeps moving and the centre visibly hands off — the figure exits or is overtaken and the frame re-centres on another person, place or event within the shot or cut.
flips.why_not: In Solid the camera returns to the same body; the privilege is stable, not momentary.

flips.if: It is Icon instead if the frame is a close-up in which the face itself is the whole image — expression cut off from space and motor outlet — rather than a person positioned as the axis of a surrounding world.
flips.why_not: Solid perception is about where perception is anchored (a body among sets, objects, others), not about a face expressing an intensity; a typical Solid shot shows the world as seen by or arranged around the subject.

flips.if: It is an opsign instead if the POV-holder is a seer who cannot act on what they see — the look no longer extends into movement or response and the scene simply overwhelms or stalls the viewer.
flips.why_not: Solid perception is the first sign of a sensory-motor world: the subject perceives in order to feel and act; the POV is linked to reverse shots and to movement.

2.name: Liquid perception
2.question: Does perception migrate?
2.gloss: the flow from character/event to character/event
2.difference: The centre moves: in a continuous reframing the shot passes from one character or environment to another, each central only until the next captures the screen.

flips.if: It is Solid instead if, however much the camera travels, it stays locked to one protagonist (a follow-shot behind one walker).
flips.why_not: A typical Liquid shot relinquishes its figure; the tracking movement is loyal to the flow, not to a person.

flips.if: It is Gaseous instead if no centre ever forms — time-lapse, superimposition, micro-shooting or manipulated stock make human figures one image among clouds, traffic and matter.
flips.why_not: In Liquid perception centres do coalesce (a character, an event), just only for a moment; the image remains human-scaled and continuous in time.

flips.if: It is Dividual instead if the travelling camera over many people is expressing one shared affect of the mass — panic, joy, grief — rather than passing attention from centre to centre.
flips.why_not: Liquid perception concerns the organisation of perception (the flow of centres), not the expression of a collective feeling; its crowds can be affectively neutral.

3.name: Gaseous perception
3.question: Can the world perceive without a human center?
3.gloss: all images resonate with one another as an acentred system
3.difference: Nothing is privileged: through slow/fast motion, superimposition, fragmentation or micro-shooting the image treats a human figure as one image like any other among landscapes, matter and machines.

flips.if: It is Liquid instead if, despite the flow, the image settles for a moment on a character or event we are invited to follow.
flips.why_not: Gaseous perception never lets a centre stabilise; its figures are not followed, they are processed.

flips.if: It is Any-space-whatever instead if the acentred space is held as an affective quality — fog, a coloured void, a ruin that expresses a mood — rather than as interacting matter-images in variation.
flips.why_not: Gaseous perception is defined by technical variation and interaction of images (speeds, superimposition); the any-space-whatever by the affect of an emptied or disconnected space, often static.

flips.if: It is an opsign instead if the acentred image is lived by a seer as a stalled situation — a character stranded before an image they can neither extend into action nor escape.
flips.why_not: Deamer places Gaseous inside the movement-image: its variation still forms an assemblage of enunciation and a conception of the whole, not a crisis of a perceiving character.

4.name: Icon
4.question: Where does intensity become a face?
4.gloss: the face expressing unfilmable internal intensities
4.difference: The face is not a feature of a person in a space but the whole image: a close-up in which expression (fixed wonder or traversing micro-movements) holds an intensity that has not yet become action.

flips.if: It is Dividual instead if the face is one of a series of faces or bodies that together express one collective emotion, the individual standing in for the mass.
flips.why_not: The Icon's intensity is concentrated in a single face; it does not depend on multiplicity.

flips.if: It is Symptom instead if the facial intensity has already tipped into a primordial act — gnawing, biting, lunging, grabbing — the face as the site of an impulse too strong for the character.
flips.why_not: The Icon suspends between perception and action (quality or power not yet actualised); the Symptom is the short-circuit where the impulse acts.

flips.if: It is Body of attitude instead if the close attention falls on the body's postures, fatigue and waiting over duration — a body that carries time — rather than on a face expressing a feeling.
flips.why_not: The Icon remains in the sensory-motor schema as affect between perception and action; body of attitude belongs to the time-image, where the body is not a centre of action at all.

5.name: Dividual
5.question: Is the feeling mine, ours, or both?
5.gloss: the conjunction of collective and individual affects
5.difference: The feeling belongs to the gathering: the crowd, pack or series of faces is individualised as one affect while each person in it is de-individualised.

flips.if: It is Icon instead if the camera isolates one face in close-up and the emotion reads as that person's own, not the crowd's reflected in them.
flips.why_not: The Dividual needs the conjunction of collective and individual; a single face alone cannot carry it unless it is shown to embody a population.

flips.if: It is Milieu instead if the mass is shown as the social situation — workers at a factory gate in an extreme wide shot establishing place, class and history — rather than as an affect.
flips.why_not: In the Dividual the crowd expresses feeling (panic, ecstasy, grief); in the Milieu it exemplifies a determined geo-historical situation.

flips.if: It is Liquid instead if the camera moving through the crowd is passing attention from one centre to the next without a shared emotional charge.
flips.why_not: A typical Dividual shot is unified by one affect traversing all bodies; the movement serves the affect, not the circulation of centres.

6.name: Any-space-whatever
6.question: Has place stopped functioning as ordinary geography?
6.difference: Affect with no face: an emptied, disconnected or amorphous space (fog, rain, shadow, coloured void, ruin, haze) that expresses a quality itself rather than locating an action.

flips.if: It is Originary world instead if the space is a determinate archetypal place — this desert, this forest, the house — charged with primal forces that are about to seize bodies, under a time of decay.
flips.why_not: Deleuze/Deamer: the originary world may resemble an any-space-whatever but appears only in the depths of a determined milieu; the any-space-whatever is indeterminate affect, not a lair of drives.

flips.if: It is an opsign instead if the space is freed from any sensory-motor linkage — no character will act on it, nothing it expresses feeds a next action — and is simply seen, with the seer stranded before it.
flips.why_not: Within the movement-image the any-space-whatever is the intensive ground of characters traversing it from perception to action; Deamer says it becomes an opsign only when set free from those linkages.

flips.if: It is Dividual instead if bodies gather in the space and the affect reads as theirs collectively rather than as the space's.
flips.why_not: The any-space-whatever is the ground out of which the dividual assembles; in its pure form the human is absent or overwhelmed.

7.name: Symptom
7.question: What force is acting through this body?
7.difference: The body acts from a drive too strong for it: a visible primordial act (devouring, rutting, seizing, cruelty) in which the human behaves as a human animal, not as an agent with a goal.

flips.if: It is Fetish instead if the charge sits in an object the body has not yet seized — the scrap, shoe, relic held in insert — and no act has discharged it.
flips.why_not: The Symptom is the discharge into a body; the Fetish is storage awaiting it.

flips.if: It is Imprint instead if the violent act is the release of pressure slowly accumulated from a complex social situation, legible through a long build and an emotional object.
flips.why_not: Deamer: the imprint's explosion 'is very different from the immediacy of the symptom'; the symptom is short-circuit, not accumulated behaviour.

flips.if: It is Icon instead if the face shows the intensity but the body stays still, the power not yet passing into an act.
flips.why_not: A typical Symptom shot shows the act itself, often bodily, often not in close-up.

8.name: Fetish
8.question: What object has become charged?
8.gloss: a special object charged with primal energies, awaiting a grounding
8.difference: A partial object is held apart and charged — relic or vult — so that the image makes us feel stored primal force in it, waiting for a body to discharge it.

flips.if: It is Imprint instead if the object is an emotional token of a social situation (a murdered child's keepsake) linking a character's accumulated grievance to a milieu, rather than a vessel of pre-moral primal force.
flips.why_not: The Fetish is prior to good and evil and outside history; the Imprint's object is a referent for a determined complex situation.

flips.if: It is Mark instead if the object's charge comes from habitual relation — it belongs to a familiar series (a cigarette case, a set of keys) and its meaning emerges when that series is recognised or broken.
flips.why_not: A Mark or Demark is an object in a web of relations for the understanding; the Fetish's meaning is 'almost automatic', a drive-charge, not a logical relation.

flips.if: It is Symptom instead if the object is already in the body's grip and the shot is about the act it compels (gnawing the meat, sniffing the shoe).
flips.why_not: The Fetish shot typically isolates the object as potential, before or apart from the discharge.

9.name: Originary world
9.question: What ancient or pre-social force underlies this milieu?
9.difference: Beneath a recognisable place rumbles an archetypal one: the forest, desert, swamp or house is shown as a determinate but timeless ground of drives and decay, not as a historical setting.

flips.if: It is Any-space-whatever instead if the space is indeterminate — a void, a fog, a colour field — expressing a pure affective quality with no specific primal place and no pressure on bodies.
flips.why_not: The originary world only appears in the depths of a determined milieu; it is a specific archetypal place with forces, not pure indeterminacy.

flips.if: It is Milieu instead if the place is historicised — dated architecture, social institutions, class markers laid out in establishing shots so actions exemplify a situation.
flips.why_not: The originary world is outside or beneath history, cyclical time, entropy; it undoes the determined milieu rather than explaining behaviour.

flips.if: It is Symptom instead if the shot's weight falls on a body already seized by the place's forces — the villager gone feral, the act of devouring — with the landscape reduced to backdrop.
flips.why_not: The Originary world is the genetic ground itself: the forces are shown in the place (its decay, cyclical time) before or beyond any single body they capture.

10.name: Index of lack
10.question: What missing situation does this action let us infer?
10.gloss: the situation is an ellipsis which is unequivocally revealed
10.difference: Something is visibly missing from the situation (an ellipsis) and the character's action fills it in one unequivocal disclosure that then redirects what they do.

flips.if: It is Index of equivocity instead if the disclosure splits — the same act or clue points to two distant situations and the film refuses to settle which.
flips.why_not: In the index of lack what is revealed is unequivocal; the reveal changes everything by determining the indeterminate.

flips.if: It is Mark/Demark instead if the revealing element is an object whose meaning comes from a habitual series being completed or broken — the thinking is done by the relation, not by the character's exploratory action.
flips.why_not: Index of lack is an action-image: the situation is deduced from the character's action, not from a relational sign offered to the spectator's understanding.

flips.if: It is Forking paths instead if the gap is filled by competing flashback versions of the past rather than by present action.
flips.why_not: The index of lack reveals a present situation through deeds; it does not branch the past.

11.name: Index of equivocity
11.question: What two worlds could explain the same action?
11.gloss: the situation is revealed as ambiguous
11.difference: An action discloses a situation that stays double: a slight difference in the same act refers it to two distant situations at once — 'this and that' — and the film sustains the undecidability.

flips.if: It is Index of lack instead if a later action resolves which situation is true and the character reorients on that single reading.
flips.why_not: The equivocal index is determined but riven; its ambiguity is a structure of the situation, not a delay before clarity.

flips.if: It is Limpid and opaque (hyalosign) instead if the doubleness is between actual and virtual — a crystal image where the undecidable is whether we see the real or its reflection/memory — rather than between two actual situations.
flips.why_not: The index of equivocity keeps both situations actual and within the sensory-motor schema; the hyalosign's indiscernibility is temporal/ontological.

flips.if: It is Powers of the false instead if incompossible versions coexist and truth itself is suspended — the narrator/character is a forger and no situation is determinable at all.
flips.why_not: Deamer insists the equivocal situation is 'no less determined'; the two poles are both true readings of one world.

12.name: Vector
12.question: How do several incomplete situations compose a world?
12.gloss: multiple situations within the homogeneous universe
12.difference: Many characters each disclose a partial, equivocal situation, and only their interlocking over the film draws the broken, unpredictable but necessary line of one world.

flips.if: It is Index of equivocity instead if the film has one principal character facing a two-sided situation rather than a multiplicity of disclosers.
flips.why_not: The Vector is a nexus of indices distributed across an ensemble; its world is heterogeneous yet homogeneous.

flips.if: It is Liquid perception instead if the ensemble is only a flow of perceived centres with no situation being disclosed by their actions.
flips.why_not: Liquid perception organises what is seen; the Vector organises what the actions reveal about a shared world.

flips.if: It is Forking paths instead if the multiple lines are alternative versions of the past told through recollection rather than simultaneous present situations.
flips.why_not: The vector's situations are 'a priori simultaneous', determined in one world; forking paths branch memory.

13.name: Milieu
13.question: What world produces these actions?
13.gloss: the situation explicated through character actions
13.difference: The situation is given before anyone acts: an establishing or extreme wide shot lays out a determined geo-historical and social space, and the people in it exemplify it rather than change it.

flips.if: It is Binomial instead if the frame is organised by two opposed forces squaring off (two camps, two lines, a standoff) so the setting is only the stage of a duel.
flips.why_not: In the Milieu the situation is foreground and action derivative (SAS, things remain as they are).

flips.if: It is Originary world instead if the place is timeless and primal — an archetypal forest or house rumbling with drives and entropy — rather than historically and socially dated.
flips.why_not: The Milieu is historicised realism; the originary world lies beneath history.

flips.if: It is Quotidian instead if the everyday life shown is a reflection-image that turns the large form around — ordinary, un-heroic banality that deflates or inverts the action form.
flips.why_not: The Milieu presents everyday existence as determined situation feeding action, without inversion or critique of the form.

14.name: Binomial
14.question: Where has the world become a duel?
14.difference: Two opposed lines of force, embodied in characters, face each other: the image is organised as a duel (violent, romantic, political) pointing toward a decisive confrontation.

flips.if: It is Milieu instead if the figures are present only as instances of their world, with no opposition structuring the frame.
flips.why_not: In the Binomial the milieu is merely the staging ground; action is foreground, 'pure action from beginning to end'.

flips.if: It is Index of equivocity instead if the two sides are two readings of one situation revealed by an act, rather than two opposed forces meeting in combat.
flips.why_not: Binomial duality is conflict between forces (S→A); equivocal duality is ambiguity of disclosure (A→S).

flips.if: It is Mirrors face to face instead if the two facing figures are doubles whose images multiply into each other, confusing actual and virtual, rather than adversaries resolving a situation.
flips.why_not: The Binomial's two poles are distinct and the duel produces a victory and a new situation (SAS′).

15.name: Imprint
15.question: How has the world gotten inside the character?
15.gloss: an indelible impression of the world upon a character
15.difference: A complex situation has entered one body: the character carries it as visible, contained pressure, often fixed on an emotional object that links them to the world, before (or as) it bursts into action.

flips.if: It is Symptom instead if the outburst is immediate and appetitive, a primal drive with no accumulated social situation behind it.
flips.why_not: Deamer: the imprint's release accumulates over the sequence and 'is very different from the immediacy of the symptom'.

flips.if: It is Icon instead if the charged face expresses a quality or power purely in itself, not as the internalisation of a determined milieu.
flips.why_not: The Imprint is an action-image: the internal state is legibly the milieu pressed into a body and destined for action.

flips.if: It is Binomial instead if the pressure is externalised as a face-off between two embodied camps, the conflict played out between characters rather than stored inside one.
flips.why_not: In the Imprint the polynomial duels are internalised in a single body; the gap between milieu and act (fifth law) is bridged slowly inside the character, and the outcome tends to deterioration (SAS″).

16.name: Plastic figure
16.question: What greater situation does this action unexpectedly imply?
16.gloss: small form transformed by the large form, an implied situation
16.difference: Does a single on-screen object, action or cut stand in, in one stroke, for a real situation that is never itself shown (metaphor/metonymy/synecdoche), while the film's own drive is still action discovering situation?

flips.if: It is Theatrical instead if the figure is not a single substituted image but a staged fictitious action (a play, game, rehearsal, parody) that runs over a sequence and prefigures a real act the film keeps deferring.
flips.why_not: A plastic figure is instantaneous and substitutive: the slaughtered bull replaces the massacre in one cut; nothing is rehearsed or deferred.

flips.if: It is a Symbol instead if the object's meaning is an abstract relation that organises the whole plot (a key, a necklace binding characters in a Hitchcockian relation) rather than a figure for a situation kept in ellipsis.
flips.why_not: The plastic figure points past itself to a real situation the film does not show; the symbol is a concrete object carrying a relation the film does show being exchanged.

flips.if: It is an Index of lack instead if the shown action is literal and simply lets us infer an unshown situation (an elision in the chain of events), with no figural substitution.
flips.why_not: The index of lack is inference from a gap; the plastic figure is a trope: the shown thing means something other than itself.

17.name: Theatrical figure
17.question: What real action is being rehearsed through fiction?
17.gloss: a sequence of images as precursor of the real action
17.difference: Is a fictitious action (performance, game, allegory, parody) being played out over a sequence as a precursor of a real action that has not yet happened and keeps being deferred?

flips.if: It is Plastic instead if the figure collapses into one substituted image or cut rather than a sustained performed sequence.
flips.why_not: The theatrical figure is linear and repeated; it needs duration and at least one repetition to prefigure.

flips.if: It is Mise en abyme instead if the performance contains figures that in turn contain the performance, so we cannot tell which level is the real action and which the rehearsal.
flips.why_not: In a theatrical figure the real/fictitious hierarchy holds: the play prefigures, the real act eventually arrives (or is known to be the thing deferred).

flips.if: It is Powers of the false instead if there is no real action the performance prefigures at all: every level is equally a forgery and truth is no longer the horizon.
flips.why_not: The theatrical figure is still a movement-image trope: it depends on a real action to come.

18.name: Mise en abyme
18.question: Is one action-world nested inside another?
18.gloss: a recurrence of plastic and theatrical figures
18.difference: Do figures nest inside figures such that, watching, you cannot say whether a performed sequence contains an emblematic image or an emblematic image contains the performed sequence?

flips.if: It is Theatrical instead if the nested performance has a clear outside: one real action that the play-within points toward.
flips.why_not: Mise en abyme loses the outside; the recursion is the point.

flips.if: It is Mirrors face to face instead if the recursion is optical, actual and virtual images exchanging in literal reflective surfaces with no trope or narrative prefiguring at stake.
flips.why_not: Mise en abyme is a recursion of figures (tropes of action and situation); the crystal is a recursion of the actual/virtual image itself, time-image not action.

flips.if: It is Powers of the false instead if the nested levels are incompossible versions with no true one and the characters are forgers of time.
flips.why_not: Mise en abyme still converts action-forms; it disorients reflection but does not abolish the true.

19.name: Figure of the sublime
19.question: Is the action bigger than the world requires?
19.gloss: actions surpass the determinates of an enfeebled situation
19.difference: Does the character's action visibly exceed anything the situation requires, so that the grandiose act makes the situation look futile (a steamship hauled over a mountain)?

flips.if: It is Enfeeblement instead if the character is small, aimless and ineffective and it is the world that swells up around them.
flips.why_not: In the sublime the character is the outsized force; the world shrinks to a futile encompasser.

flips.if: It is Milieu instead if the situation determines and justifies the heroic response, a large-form SAS where action answers the milieu and modifies it.
flips.why_not: The sublime action is not required by the situation; the ratio between act and givens is broken.

flips.if: It is an Imprint instead if the excess is interior and explained: a psychological obsession or buried drive drives the act and the film reads it as character causality.
flips.why_not: The sublime is hallucinatory and visionary; the act exposes the situation as absurd rather than exposing the character's hidden motive.

20.name: Figure of enfeeblement
20.question: Is the actor tiny compared with the world disclosed?
20.gloss: weak characters reveal the sublime nature of the world
20.difference: Do a weak character's small, futile acts make an immense, indifferent world swell into view (the tiny point fleeing to the horizon), rather than the world merely sitting there?

flips.if: It is Quotidian instead if the small acts are neither futile nor merely revelatory but carry their own petty heroism, so trivial and immense can't be separated.
flips.why_not: Enfeeblement keeps the inversion one-way: the act is futile, the world is sublime.

flips.if: It is an Opsign instead if the character no longer acts at all (a seer, not a weakling doing something) and the situation is a pure optical one cut from any sensory-motor response.
flips.why_not: The enfeebled still acts, however feebly; the small form is inverted, not broken.

flips.if: It is Any-space-whatever instead if the vast space is emptied or disconnected and carries affect in itself, with no character action measuring it.
flips.why_not: Enfeeblement needs the weakling's act as the measure that reveals the grandiose; remove the act and it becomes affection.

21.name: Quotidian
21.question: Has everyday life become both ridiculous and heroic?
21.gloss: everyday situations, everyday actions – sublime ↔ futile
21.difference: Is an everyday act shown so that you cannot decide whether it is trivial or heroic, the situation both inconsequential and unfathomable at once?

flips.if: It is Enfeeblement instead if the act reads plainly as futile and the world plainly as overwhelming.
flips.why_not: In the quotidian the petty function is itself the heroism; neither pole dominates.

flips.if: It is an Opsign instead if the everyday is shown as a pure optical situation where no one can act at all (Ozu's empty vase, still lifes) rather than as an act of duty.
flips.why_not: The quotidian is still an action-figure: the character works, serves, carries on.

flips.if: It is Body of attitude instead if the everyday is carried by the tired, waiting body whose postures express time, and action has dropped out.
flips.why_not: The quotidian is about the ambivalent value of action, not the body's time.

22.name: Limit of the large form action-image
22.question: What hidden question does this world contain?
22.difference: Before acting, does the character have to extract a question hidden in the situation (what is a samurai now?), so action is delayed into a considered response rather than an explosive reaction?

flips.if: It is the Small-form limit instead if there is no given situation holding a question; the question is assembled from heterogeneous actions and stays unanswered.
flips.why_not: In Ll the milieu is given and the question is a priori; a response is eventually possible.

flips.if: It is Milieu instead if the situation simply provokes the character to a direct reply (SAS) with no pause to formulate its question.
flips.why_not: Ll suspends the duel/response in favour of investigating the situation's givens.

flips.if: It is the Extreme limit instead if you can't tell whether the problem came from the situation or from the actions, and the whole world has become a cipher of forces.
flips.why_not: Ll still has a determinate milieu and a direction toward answer.

23.name: Limit of the small form action-image
23.question: Why do the clues refuse to settle the situation?
23.gloss: the situation revealed as a problem
23.difference: Do parallel, heterogeneous lines of action connect only as pieces from different puzzles, so the situation they reveal remains an unanswered cipher, a sustained ellipsis?

flips.if: It is the Large-form limit instead if a single given milieu poses the question and a considered response closes it.
flips.why_not: Ls has no originating situation; action cannot disclose one.

flips.if: It is an Index of equivocity instead if a single action points ambiguously to two possible situations and the film eventually decides between them.
flips.why_not: Equivocity is a doubled reading of one situation; Ls is many incongruent lines whose sum is a question.

flips.if: It is Forking paths instead if the heterogeneous lines are memories, flashbacks within flashbacks that never reconcile.
flips.why_not: Ls is a present-tense action structure, not a structure of recollection.

24.name: Limit of the action-image (extreme limit)
24.question: Has action itself stopped being an adequate solution?
24.difference: Is the film permeated by problems from start to end so that you can no longer tell whether they are posed by the situation or discovered by action, the world itself appearing as a field of indeterminate forces?

flips.if: It is the Small-form limit instead if the question is still traceable to the characters' actions building a cipher, with a clear action-to-situation direction.
flips.why_not: Xl collapses the direction; the originary form is undecidable.

flips.if: It is Any-space-whatever instead if the space is encountered as pure affect (quality/power) with no problem being worked through by action or thought.
flips.why_not: Xl is the return to the any-space-whatever inside thought: action is still interrogating, now ungrounded.

flips.if: It is an Opsign instead if action has actually broken down and characters only see and hear.
flips.why_not: Xl is the limit of action-images still within the movement-image; the characters still pursue a problem.

25.name: Rich dream
25.question: Can we clearly tell when the dream begins?
25.gloss: radically distinct real world and dream world
25.difference: Is the passage into the dream explicitly marked and ornately made (dissolves, superimpositions, effects), with an equally marked exit, so the dream is attributed to a dreamer and recognised as dream by the viewer?

flips.if: It is Restrained instead if entry is a straight cut and the dream looks like concrete everyday reality with only an uncanny slip.
flips.why_not: The rich dream announces itself: 'This is a dream!'

flips.if: It is Strong destiny instead if the marked dissolve leads not into an impossible world but into a realistic past event that then determines the character's action.
flips.why_not: A rich dream's content is impossible and abstracting; a flashback's content is a past that happened.

flips.if: It is Mirrors face to face instead if the superimposition/reflection doesn't lead into a dreamer's world but makes actual and virtual images endlessly exchange with no one dreaming.
flips.why_not: The rich dream has a dreamer and a return; the crystal has no subject-anchored entry or exit.

26.name: Restrained dream
26.question: Are we unsure whether waking has ended?
26.gloss: an ambiguity between real world and dream world
26.difference: Is the dream entered by an invisible cut and made of concrete everyday things with one impossible unhinging, so that the film's task becomes deciding whether we are awake?

flips.if: It is Rich instead if the entry is ornate and the imagery overtly strange.
flips.why_not: The restrained dream hides its marking; you only learn it was a dream afterward, if ever.

flips.if: It is Weak destiny instead if the unmarked intrusion turns out to be a past event (an incomplete memory) rather than an impossible present.
flips.why_not: Restrained dream content is impossible or uncanny; weak-destiny content is a real past, just fragmentary.

flips.if: It is Powers of the false instead if the ambiguity is never meant to be resolved and no dreamer anchors it: real and imaginary are undecidable in principle.
flips.why_not: The restrained dream is still attributed to a dreamer and the film works to separate dream from real.

27.name: Movement of world
27.question: What if nobody ever wakes up?
27.gloss: the dream world is the real world
27.difference: Is there no entry or exit at all: does the world itself carry the character along (song, dance, impossible events treated as natural) so that no one is the dreamer?

flips.if: It is Rich instead if the number or fantasy is framed as a character's reverie with a marked return to a non-musical reality.
flips.why_not: In movement of world the fantasy is the reality; there is nothing outside it.

flips.if: It is Body of gest instead if the bodies' theatricalised ceremony or gesture creates the time and nothing requires a world-movement to supplant the character's action.
flips.why_not: Movement of world is a movement-image: the world's movement takes over the character's faltering motor act.

flips.if: It is Seed and environment instead if the enchanted world is a crystal that grows from a seed and is closed, time-crystallised (e.g. a stage world that the crystal contains) rather than a dream-circuit of anamorphoses.
flips.why_not: Movement of world is still a mental-image of the dream, with a sensory-motor subject carried along.

28.name: Strong destiny
28.question: Does the remembered past command what happens next?
28.gloss: a flashback to the past determines the future
28.difference: Does a marked flashback (pause, dissolve, monochrome, reverb) return to the present and pass through affect into an action it determines, closing a causal circuit?

flips.if: It is Weak destiny instead if the flashback is unmarked or incomplete and settles into the present's mood without yet driving an act.
flips.why_not: Strong destiny's past is clear and it fuels a decisive act.

flips.if: It is a Rich dream instead if the marked transition opens onto impossible, transformed imagery rather than a realistic past.
flips.why_not: Strong destiny's content is what happened.

flips.if: It is Sheets of the past instead if we move among coexisting regions of the past, none decisive, with no single recollection closing a circuit to action.
flips.why_not: Strong destiny uses the past to explain; sheets explore the past as virtual coexistence.

29.name: Weak destiny
29.question: Does memory color the present without dictating it?
29.gloss: the content of the flashback permeates affects
29.difference: Is the flashback ambiguous, incomplete or shared, so it saturates present feeling as a clue to an ellipsis that must be reconstructed before any action can follow?

flips.if: It is Strong destiny instead if the flashback is clearly marked and complete and directly produces an action.
flips.why_not: Weak destiny stalls action; the past is a puzzle, not a cause.

flips.if: It is a Restrained dream instead if the unmarked intrusion is impossible rather than a past event.
flips.why_not: Weak destiny content is real past, fragmentary.

flips.if: It is Sheets of the past instead if no ellipsis is ultimately resolved and the film moves among coexisting ages of the past without a present to rescue.
flips.why_not: Weak destiny still aims at reconstruction and resolution.

30.name: Forking paths
30.question: Which past, if any, actually explains the present?
30.difference: Do flashbacks fork within flashbacks, irreconcilably, so the past is explored for its own sake as an inexplicable secret and psychological causality is shown to be a ruse?

flips.if: It is Weak destiny instead if the fragments eventually cohere and resolve the present ellipsis.
flips.why_not: Forking paths never reconcile; the secret remains.

flips.if: It is Sheets of the past instead if the forking no longer passes through flashbacks at all but directly through coexistent regions of pure past, with no present anchoring the recollections.
flips.why_not: Forking paths is still a movement-image of memory: actualised flashbacks returning to a present.

flips.if: It is Powers of the false instead if the contradictory versions are not memories of a secret but forgeries that make truth itself undecidable.
flips.why_not: Forking paths assumes a past that happened, just unreachable.

31.name: Mark
31.question: What recurring thing has become meaningful because it repeats?
31.gloss: the relation between a habitual series of images
31.difference: Can you point to at least three occurrences of the same image or motif that the characters or viewer come to read as one habitual series with a meaning to be deciphered?

flips.if: It is a demark instead if the shot shows one instance that breaks the established series: wrong place, wrong form, wrong time.
flips.why_not: A mark shot confirms the series; it adds one more regular term and nothing in it is out of pattern.

flips.if: It is mise en abyme instead if the repetition nests one image inside another (a picture of the film within the film) instead of lining up terms in time.
flips.why_not: The mark's repetitions follow one another as separate perceived objects in the present, not images framed inside images.

flips.if: It is sheets of the past instead if the recurring image returns the viewer to different, non-chronological layers of the past rather than building a logical inference.
flips.why_not: The mark stays in the present and in logic ('because', 'therefore'); its recurrences point forward to an interpretation, not back into strata of time.

32.name: Demark
32.question: What breaks the pattern?
32.gloss: an aberration in the series of habitual images
32.difference: Does the shot show a known term of an established series appearing out of place or contradicting that series, so that the aberration itself shocks thought?

flips.if: It is a mark instead if the term appears where and as the series predicts.
flips.why_not: The demark is defined by violation; a conforming instance only restates the series.

flips.if: It is an index of equivocity instead if the shot presents one action that can be read two ways, with no prior habitual series being broken.
flips.why_not: The demark needs a pattern set up earlier in the film; its shock comes from the pattern, not from an ambiguity in the action.

flips.if: It is powers of the false instead if the break undoes the truth of the whole narration (a storyteller exposed, versions multiplying) and no pattern is left to restore.
flips.why_not: A demark breaks a series inside a logic that still holds, and thought re-orients; the powers of the false erode the ground of truth itself.

33.name: Symbol
33.question: What idea is being thought through this thing?
33.gloss: an object expressing ideas, beliefs, concepts
33.difference: Is a single concrete object held on screen as the knot where several separate threads of the film's relations meet, so that it carries an idea, belief or concept rather than a use or a desire?

flips.if: It is a fetish instead if the object is invested with drive (grabbed, hoarded, torn at, possessed) in an originary world of impulse.
flips.why_not: The symbol is thought about, not clutched: its value is abstract relation, not an object of predatory drive.

flips.if: It is a mark instead if the object only recurs as one term of a single habitual series.
flips.why_not: The symbol gathers demarks from several different series into one object; a mark belongs to one line of repetition.

flips.if: It is a lectosign instead if what must be read is the whole film's image, narration and narrative with no single object given as the key.
flips.why_not: The symbol offers a key object that settles meaning inside the movement-image; a lectosign offers no key, only a relinking the viewer must do.

34a.name: Opsign
34a.question: Can this sight still be discharged into action?
34a.gloss: the zeroness of the time-image: a pure optical situation
34a.difference: With the sound off, is the image something to be seen and nothing more: no one's goal organises it, what moves in it resolves nothing, and the look is not converted into action?

flips.if: It is (also or only) a sonsign if the sound carries the situation, holding the scene while the image is neutral, dark or incidental.
flips.why_not: A typical opsign still stands with the sound off; its pure situation is visual.

flips.if: It is an any-space-whatever instead if the disconnected space works as the ground of affect (shadow, colour, emptiness charging a feeling in a movement-image film) and the film then goes back into action.
flips.why_not: The opsign is the any-space-whatever after the movement-image has collapsed: the space no longer charges a later affect or act but is simply seen.

flips.if: It is the quotidian instead if everyday banality is framed as a critical figure (a reflection on routine) inside a film still driven by situation → action.
flips.why_not: The opsign does not comment on the everyday; the look just stalls on it, and the film does not return to a plot the banality serves.

34b.name: Sonsign
34b.question: Does this sound stand alone as a situation, answered by no action?
34b.gloss: the zeroness of the time-image: a pure sound situation
34b.difference: With the image covered, does a sound hold the scene as a situation in itself, not score, not plot-driving dialogue, not a cue someone answers?

flips.if: It is an opsign instead if the shot still stands with the sound off and the sound is just ambient support.
flips.why_not: In a sonsign the image is neutral, dark or frozen; take the sound away and the situation disappears.

flips.if: It is a mark instead if the sound recurs (a bell, a whistle, a ringtone) as a habitual series that characters interpret as a clue.
flips.why_not: The sonsign does not point anywhere; it is heard, not deciphered, and nothing is inferred from it.

flips.if: It is an action-image sign (binomial: situation → response) instead if the sound triggers a response: the alarm makes someone run, the phone is answered, the whistle ends the shift.
flips.why_not: A sonsign has no motor extension; the listener stays frozen or absent and the sound outlasts any reaction.

35.name: Mirrors face to face
35.question: Which image is original?
35.difference: Does one body or thing appear in the same shot as several reflections or doubles at once (facing, angled or distorting mirrors, glass), so that actual and virtual can no longer be told apart?

flips.if: It is limpid and opaque instead if, over time, one side clears as the other clouds (a reflection fades as the room behind the glass appears, or the reverse).
flips.why_not: Mirrors face to face multiply simultaneously; there is no passage from clear to obscure, just many images at once.

flips.if: It is mise en abyme instead if the image framed within the image is a representation (a painting, a play, a screen) reflecting the story critically.
flips.why_not: In the mirror image the doubles are the body itself dispersed, not a representation of the plot within the plot.

flips.if: It is a theatrical figure instead if the mirror is just a stage prop for a role or disguise being performed and then taken off.
flips.why_not: Mirrors face to face make the self crystalline and fragmented; there is no 'real' self to return to after the play.

36.name: Limpid and opaque
36.question: Which side of the image is becoming real?
36.gloss: the exchange of the actual and virtual
36.difference: During the shot or scene, does one face of the image clear (becomes visible or real) while the other clouds (becomes obscure or virtual), so that the two sides keep changing places?

flips.if: It is mirrors face to face instead if the doubles are all present at once and nothing passes from clear to opaque.
flips.why_not: The limpid/opaque is a passage in time (an exchange), not a simultaneous multiplication.

flips.if: It is powers of the false instead if what alternates is the truth of the whole story (a performer versus a real witness, with no fact left) rather than two faces of one image.
flips.why_not: The limpid/opaque exchanges actual and virtual within an image or scene; the powers of the false dissolve truth across the narration.

flips.if: It is a rich dream instead if the obscure side is marked as a character's dream with a clear waking frame around it.
flips.why_not: In the limpid/opaque the virtual is not assigned to a dreamer's head; reality and virtual pass into each other without a frame.

37.name: Seed and environment
37.question: What future world lies virtually inside this image?
37.difference: Is there a small enclosed image (a snow globe, model, miniature stage, a drop, a crystal) that contains in germ the world that surrounds it or will grow from it, with seed and environment reversible?

flips.if: It is limpid and opaque instead if two faces trade places over time without one containing the other.
flips.why_not: Seed and environment is a relation of enclosure and growth (small holds large), not alternation.

flips.if: It is mise en abyme instead if the inner image is a critical reflection (story within story) that the plot comments on and then leaves.
flips.why_not: The seed is not a commentary but a germ: the environment grows out of it or collapses back into it, and you cannot say which is primary.

flips.if: It is cinema of the brain instead if the whole set or world is laid out as a mental map with no enclosed miniature seed.
flips.why_not: The seed/environment keeps a germinal object inside the world; the brain-cinema turns the whole screen into the cerebral space.

38.name: Peaks of the present
38.question: What if several presents are simultaneously valid?
38.difference: Does the narration give several different presents at once (a present of the past, a present of the present, a present of the future) in the same event, without flashback framing to rank them?

flips.if: It is sheets of the past instead if the coexistence is of strata of the past explored as a memory-world, not of presents.
flips.why_not: Peaks of the present are simultaneous nows (the same moment lived as several), not layers dug back into.

flips.if: It is forking paths instead if the alternatives are subordinated to one present (a flashback that explains, or possibilities that resolve into one timeline).
flips.why_not: In peaks of the present no version is the frame; the presents are incompossible yet all actual.

flips.if: It is the limit of large form instead if parallel lines of action converge in a race to a decisive duel.
flips.why_not: The peaks do not converge on an act; they stay heterogeneous and unresolved.

39.name: Sheets of the past
39.question: Which layer of the past are we inhabiting?
39.gloss: the non-chronological nature of the past
39.difference: Does the film move between regions of the past that coexist and ricochet non-chronologically (layered periods in one space, without a present-day narrator motivating each return)?

flips.if: It is peaks of the present instead if what coexists are nows, not strata of the past.
flips.why_not: Sheets of the past are the past as a whole, sheet on sheet, into which the film plunges.

flips.if: It is a recollection-image (strong destiny) instead if a flashback is motivated by a character's present need and returns to that present.
flips.why_not: The sheets are not summoned to explain the present; there is no cause and effect, only ricochet.

flips.if: It is a milieu instead if the historical setting is a determining environment for present action.
flips.why_not: In the sheets the historical space is a memory-world traversed, not a situation to be acted on.

40.name: Powers of the false
40.question: What if contradiction generates rather than obstructs the story?
40.gloss: serialism, the ongoing ungrounding of the image
40.difference: Does the film expose its own claim to truth, with testimony, performance or versions that pass into one another so that no image can be held as the true one?

flips.if: It is limpid and opaque instead if the exchange is local to one image (the glass, the role) and the narration's truth is not at stake.
flips.why_not: The powers of the false act on the series of the narration, not on one image's two faces.

flips.if: It is a theatrical figure instead if the deception is a role inside a stable plot that is eventually unmasked.
flips.why_not: The powers of the false have no unmasking: there is no underlying truth to reveal.

flips.if: It is a demark instead if one aberrant item breaks a logic that is then restored by thinking it through.
flips.why_not: The powers of the false do not re-orient a logic; they make falsification itself the process.

41.name: Bodies of attitude
41.question: What does the body think before it acts?
41.gloss: a dispersed individuation of the body
41.difference: Is the body shown waiting, tired, slumped or posing, in its everydayness, with the posture itself as the content and no act prepared or completed?

flips.if: It is a body of gest instead if attitudes are linked into a performed social gesture addressed or staged (Brechtian demonstration, ritual, choreographed routine).
flips.why_not: Attitude is the body before linkage; the gest strings attitudes into a social act.

flips.if: It is the quotidian instead if everyday life is framed as a critical figure inside a film still ruled by action.
flips.why_not: In the body of attitude the everyday posture becomes the site of thought, not a comment within a plot.

flips.if: It is enfeeblement instead if the lassitude is the waning of a character's ability to act, measured against actions still expected.
flips.why_not: The body of attitude is not failing to act; action is simply not its register.

42.name: Bodies of gest
42.question: How do postures become social relations?
42.gloss: the linkage of attitudes creating differentiation
42.difference: Are postures chained into a visible, repeated or staged gesture that performs a social act (ritual, bureaucratic routine, demonstration) and is shown as performance, not as efficient action?

flips.if: It is a body of attitude instead if the body stays in one posture with no linkage into a performed act.
flips.why_not: The gest links; the attitude rests.

flips.if: It is a theatrical figure instead if the performance is a character's disguise or play that serves a plot.
flips.why_not: The gest is the social act of the body itself exhibited, not a mask worn for a narrative end.

flips.if: It is an imprint instead if the gesture is the milieu's mark on the body, leading to action within the large form.
flips.why_not: The gest does not convert into action on the world; it is exhibited as gesture.

43.name: Cinema of the brain
43.question: Has the screen itself become a thinking system?
43.gloss: the screen as a cerebral space
43.difference: Is the set or world laid out as a map of thought (abstract floor plans, chalk-drawn spaces, landscapes as mental states), so that the screen reads as a brain rather than a place to act in?

flips.if: It is seed and environment instead if a miniature germ inside the world contains it, rather than the whole screen being the mental space.
flips.why_not: The brain-cinema has no inner crystal; the whole field is cerebral.

flips.if: It is a milieu instead if the environment determines characters' behaviour as a real situation to resolve.
flips.why_not: The brain-screen's spaces do not determine action; they are thought itself topologised.

flips.if: It is gaseous perception instead if the image dissolves into acentred molecular movement (flicker, particles) without organising a mental map.
flips.why_not: The cinema of the brain is highly organised; it is thought's architecture, not matter's dispersal.

44.name: Lectosigns
44.question: What must I read here that I cannot simply see?
44.difference: Does grasping the film require you to relink its images, narration and narrative yourself, because none of them links 'naturally' and no single key object resolves it?

flips.if: It is a symbol instead if an object hands the viewer a key that settles the meaning.
flips.why_not: The lectosign offers no key; reading is relinking across the whole film.

flips.if: It is the extreme limit instead if the difficulty is a proliferation of problems within a plot of action that the film itself poses and works through.
flips.why_not: The lectosign's reading is not a problem the film sets and pursues; it opens onto what the film does not think.

flips.if: It is (only) the cinema of the brain instead if one domain, the world as brain, carries the demand without frame, shot, montage, colour and sound all requiring reading.
flips.why_not: The lectosign is the limit of all time-images together, not one noosign.

ligands.name: Poet
ligands.what: RY reading her own lines: the spring every other voice is measured from (poet_dist 1.0, f0 111 Hz).
ligands.law: Owns the front. Never cut, never ducked, never covered: everything else yields to her.

ligands.name: Whisper
ligands.what: The poet's voice in fragments: 439 power-phrase chops and breaths, her words as material.
ligands.law: Only in her silences (≥ 3.5 s gap), 18 s apart; never over a word of hers.

ligands.name: Kin
ligands.what: Mouths nearest the poet (poet_dist < 7.5): narration kin singing her lines.
ligands.law: Waits for her line to end and ≥ 2 s of quiet; then answers. Drops to 0.12 if she returns.

ligands.name: Mouth
ligands.what: Other singers carrying her lines, further from the poet (dist ≥ 7.5), by register ABYSSAL / DEEP / LOW / HIGH.
ligands.law: Same law as Kin, one step lower: never two mouths at once.

ligands.name: Chorus
ligands.what: Many mouths at once: combined codex lines, the crowd singing the poem.
ligands.law: Only in gaps and endings; the codas. A chorus under her is a collision.

ligands.name: Found voice
ligands.what: Strangers speaking in the archive footage: narrators, instructors, voices of the films themselves.
ligands.law: An archive voice never speaks over hers: under her words it drops to 0.12; alone it may lead.

ligands.name: Song
ligands.what: Sections of the 34 carrier songs (744 segments, 19 families): the poem's own music.
ligands.law: One music at a time. Under her voice: mid-band carved (−7 dB at 1.4 kHz), bus to 10%.

ligands.name: Loop
ligands.what: Rhythm: 60 mined loops on a bar grid (median 2.56 s, flatness 0.008 — the most tonal thing in the atlas).
ligands.law: Enters on a bar; matches tempo by playback rate; yields to any voice by carving, not stopping.

ligands.name: Stem
ligands.what: Orchestra chairs: single instruments from the songs (drums, piano, synth, vocals, bass, strings).
ligands.law: A chair in the poem's key (root or fifth) may stay under her; other keys wait for the gap.

ligands.name: Found music
ligands.what: Music inside the archive footage: scores, radios, bands of the found films.
ligands.law: One music at a time: two musics crossfade on a beat, or the later one sinks to texture (lowpass, −12 dB).

ligands.name: Drone
ligands.what: The unified drone: the corpus clock itself (1,440.1 s), and drone keynotes.
ligands.law: Never leaves. Under her 0.045, in breaths 0.09, after her 0.13 (the water table's key-bed).

ligands.name: Bed
ligands.law: Keynote: ducks under every voice (1 − 0.9·amt, 30 ms down, 160 ms up).

ligands.name: Texture
ligands.what: Textures: 30 noisy segments (flatness 0.74, centroid 3.5 kHz — the noisiest element).
ligands.law: Lowest priority of the field: first to go when two things fight.

ligands.name: Found noise
ligands.what: Noise and effects in the archive footage: machines, traffic, rooms, weather.
ligands.law: Normalised to −24 LUFS; ducks under voices; removing it shrinks the off-screen space (Deamer p.168).

ligands.name: Riser
ligands.law: Aims at a cut: ends on the next cut or breath; never rises into her word.

ligands.name: Hit
ligands.law: Snaps to the next silence ≥ 1 s within 3 s; at least 7 s apart; never on a word.

ligands.name: Silence
ligands.what: The gap: her 606 breaths and pauses, and the archive's silent shots. The zero of the table.
ligands.law: Silence is placed, not left: the one element nothing may enter unless the law allows it.

catalysts.name: Drop the score
catalysts.does: remove the music: the image loses its instructions

catalysts.name: Drop the effects
catalysts.does: remove the noise: the off-screen space closes

catalysts.name: Unnatural voice
catalysts.does: theatrical, text-heavy, swamped or unsubtitled speech: the voice stops belonging to a body

catalysts.name: Expose the lock
catalysts.does: put a sound IN against a picture that did not make it: synchresis shown as a contract

poems.title: OUT OF LIFE
poems.tagline: the maze, the haze, the fall, the ember
poems.logline: A poet reads aloud to a lover's turned back; the vape haze claims the room, the lover falls off the fire escape, and the poet falls behind — out of life — until it gets as dark as black.
poems.thesis: The way out he searches for (hallways, drawers, fire escapes) is the way down; leaving is not an exit but a direction.
poems.tone: Close, dim and withholding; yearning becomes spatial distance.

lines.text: What we've made we don't want, what we've sold to the world, to ourselves, doesn't exist.
I look for a way out through the hallways, within the drawers and fire escapes, trip
on my own words, falling out of life, and find where you go when you leave.
It was the maze constructed by a tainted love, a known yet unknown pit beneath the quicksands
of the make-believe haven, and hidden in the overnourished forest of escapism that calls
for you.
At this age, I'll follow, following the full distance between us almost having it all and
starting anew, to rediscover when love was real.
I failed at protecting you from your own vices, crashing the party of your evilest instincts
to find vibrations that echo in silence, love and hate languages that translate and slow
dripping blood salivating on imminent doubts, fully awakening to our darkest nights.
Pause for a second, a spectrum of fields will thread needles of garments made of sweet memories
and photographs, film and fiction that leave me empty.
With your back faced against me, you offer me a new pursuit of happiness as I stumble
on my own words, landing into the secret of where you go when you leave, and I fall
out of life.

poems.title: FLASHING LIGHTS
poems.logline: Floating in black between caving walls, a poet's eyes dilate until the pupil swallows the frame — and inside is age six: a window, a winding road, arguing headlights, a ghost with a tambourine, and the first throw.
poems.thesis: The silent scream and the silent call are the same instrument; the tambourine is the first time the poet answers noise with noise.
poems.tone: Hard light against black; vulnerability alternates with sensory assault.

lines.text: I heard a scream for help while falling with my headlights off.
It was a type of silent scream a trap lover makes to escape a pending marriage,
a concussion, a set of walls caving inward, seething and simmering,
and a solitude of crowds and smiles.
I received an emergency call while tossing and turning.
It was a type of silent call a man makes to the mirror after midnight.
To digest the truth, a windless insomnia and epiphany of a road winding down.
After a day of life dilated at the sun as long and as wise as possible, we won't make it.
I was six I recall when the ghost of a dead and loveless seven-year-old child appeared
and shared that my parents marriage wouldn't last.
It was a type of warm and heavy breeze in winter
where a child is left home alone.
With curtains pulled and blinds up as far and as wise as possible to see flashing lights
and the whispering screams of two souls on a road winding down.
And no tears and no fucks, no love to give, old to teach.

poems.logline: The tambourine thrown at age six flies into a chapel still whole, waits at the altar step through the cobwebs, and a time-lapse storm takes the building down to two stubs and a doorway — then the storm ends, the film turns white, and the tambourine falls one last time and shatters among two sets of footprints.
poems.thesis: An engagement is broken the way a chapel decays: first the cross tilts, then the roof, then the register of the world itself — and the gift that started it all only breaks after everything it was thrown at is gone.
poems.tone: Abandoned ceremonial space; decay gives way to a pale, emptied shore.

lines.text: Old to forever, a tambourine sounds off an empty temple, empty choir stands, empty prayer lines, and abandoned Baptist pools,
pews taken by cobwebs, and doused in disintegration.
Spirits have left salvations and opened gift boxes placed outside the side doors.
It thunders, then it rains until nothing remains.
Old to the storm ending, what was once love now goods,
broken and sealed apart by lightning,
daily breads soaked and delivered rotted by rain,
and blankets soiled by venomous puppeteers,
old to two sets of button-printed footsteps,
and a tambourine shattered into pieces.

poems.title: NEVERMORE
poems.tagline: a trail followed twice, a vow made twice
poems.logline: In red and black, hands in pockets, a poet walks the shore of everything that broke, lets a heart lift itself back into his chest, follows the trail into a night that falls through the film's own register, and searches a bare field until his hands — they too used to be his — return, and the arms are drawn for the first time.
poems.thesis: Recovery is not retrieval: the heart and the hands come back on their own terms, and the self's only work is to walk, kneel, and receive — nevermore said once per organ.
poems.tone: Patient and solitary; small false glints delay the bodily restoration.
symbols: Throbbing heart/Familiar heart/Reclaimed heart/Dusk settled heart
Moonlit night’s garden fields/Golden hue plants

lines.text: What if I follow this trail to where the broken pieces have washed ashore and the ashes of expired wildfires
cover sands and debris
lift it from the night seawater's floor.
The waves will calm to fold it whispers and the winds will mute the trees for the right level of silence
to find a throbbing heart left at the midlife corner returned toward the incline.
A familiar heart
which has shaken off every sad blue note life can perform
to overcome and spread inspiration
and it used to be mine. I'll lift it with care putting it back in place and tell myself
nevermore.
What if I follow this reclaimed heart to where the puzzle pieces of faith are handcrafted
scrambled and scattered as mustard seas into the vast moonlight night's field.
The plants in a golden hue bloom and face toward me in anticipation.
The weeds repel falling into the shadows where our memories hide and mean so little in moments of defeat
as I'm called forward.
The clouds meet the stars for the deepest level of darkness welcoming extra hard work
to search for the bare ground for two hands. Hands that once could tusk dusk after dusk
find and celebrate a new life and feel good
and they too used to be mine.
I put them back on with the care of my future at stake and say to myself
nevermore. I've wanted the world and lost my soul.
I want nothing more than to just be myself and nothing more
and be alright. I do believe I'll be alright.
This reclaimed and dust settled heart rediscovered but dusted hands remind me
but say to me in this still muted tree in night garden feels silence
nevermore.
Now go.

poems.title: BLOODLINES
poems.tagline: he names the stars after the people who made him
poems.logline: Told NOW GO, the poet walks into a parade of crowned ancestors who hand him stars to name, lower a galaxy into his returned hands, hover his basement childhood in the sky as a white lit room, run their blood through his fingerprint whorls until his voice drops to a baritone of a million cries — and open marble gates with wings to welcome him through.
poems.thesis: Inheritance is not received but conducted: the blood is an orchestra, the stars take new names, and the gates only open for a body that has already gotten its heart and hands back.
poems.tone: Solemn inheritance with growing defiance; scale expands from body to cosmos.
symbols: Deepening voice/Baritone of a million cries/Unanswered plight

lines.text: They tell me to ask if I can inherit the earth,
to ask if I can name my own stars, even galaxies if I may.
The past too was waiting for me.
Coming of age in the shared rooms of human basements
as bedrooms, mattress pads where the wood beams
of southern pine could comfort my spine, it didn't.
To dream was to prevail.
They tell me to ask if I can invent a new universe,
to ask if God would let me, little old me,
award a blessing here or there.
Even grant miracles where the needs
of the spoken word exists.
In uncertain times, in forsaken times,
in tears that spoke in lieu of forbidden lines,
or a history too battered and bruised to travel.
To dream was to prevail.
Their blood flows through my hands.
Fingerprints that orchestra great powers,
they tell me, sun kissing my skin
and deepening my voice to a baritone of a million cries,
to an unanswered plight.
Beware of me.

poems.title: RESURRECTING ATLANTIS
poems.tagline: a city comes up out of the water
poems.logline: Down a road that lights its own bricks, past comets all pointing one way, the poet watches a drowned city let go of its water, pays the gate with one of his named stars, wanders streets where every joyful noise blooms a rainbow, stands in a plaza until the whole city blinks with his heart — and follows the music into a house.
poems.thesis: A city born in unison out of the purest of fictions is entered the way faith is: you pay with something you were just given a name for, and the light at the door costs you your own.
poems.tone: Expansive, serene and welcoming; belonging is expressed through shared rhythms.

lines.text: The gates open with wings gifted from evolution, and made of marble stones
kissed by the hymns our creator composed with an orchestra of our ancestors wildest dreams to
welcome us. Poets who eased generations down yellow brick roads and plucked our souls out
of their secret places to follow comets to the capital city of our collective consciousness,
resurrecting Atlantis. Here we are all one. The pack we've made here with nature
abandon and hope for the best back on life. A relearned currency we reassess as a mission,
but here we are all safe. Here we are all one. The pack we've made here with nature
abandon and hope for the best back on life. A relearned currency we reassess as a mission,
but here we are all safe. An unfamiliar flickering candlelight illuminating smiles
at night where shadows cast from narrow streets beaming with love, and the joyful noises that
color rainbows, and give us infinite time to heal and set clouds free. I know my soul and
it could stay here forever, leaving behind crosshairs for continuums and strains for
serendipity. A city born in unison out of the purest of fictions welcoming me and welcoming all.

poems.title: DJ TURN ME UP
poems.logline: A DJ is lowered into the house on a beam of light, the needle rings the room, and the poet — eyes wide shut, chin nested down — tells the whole love story over a rising fader: ghosts in vineyards, rings diverging, a home trucked apart, eleven petals plunked off a daisy, three roads and one silver lining — until the chin nests high and the volume clips.
poems.thesis: Being heard is a gain structure: the same story at level one is grief and at level eight is testimony — the fader, not the words, is what turns forth to face delights and shadows.
poems.tone: Exposed and insistent; the performance moves from lowered chin to claimed voice.

lines.text: DJ turn me up please. With eyes wide shut and my chin nested at the arc of the weight of these
spoken words, I have a story to tell. Of ghosts whispering unfolded delusions, birthed in purity
and dying and the veneers of sun-soaked evergreen fields are nourished. A love story of one by one
treasures escaping and devaluing themselves after defamed unsalted stars diminish their glares.
And I've walked a thousand light years across the greatest divide to be heard. So DJ please turn me
up. So I can speak of wedding bands diverging across abstract skies of wounded souls. Of a
shared home boxed in truck on separate one-way streets not built with u-turns or stop. Maybe
we shouldn't signs. A love story of years 11 years each plucked off as daisy pedals
we love we not. Of a future gone swiftly and a past left empty handed to pick a road of heavy rain
or a frontal fog or of dim night lights under a cloud with the silver lining. Of now turning
forth to face the lights and shadows one night at a time, one tear at a time. When called to a friend
at a time. One open mic at a time. Chin now nested high and volume turned up in a story to tell.

poems.title: NEWLY SINGLE
poems.tagline: a soul leaves a body on a dance floor
poems.logline: On a rooftop running faster than its own night, the poet's soul steps out of his body, watches all of Atlantis top-down, stands at the equator of a hotter planet, lets angels pour moon-salted ice baths over the husk he left dancing — then returns, leans back, breathes the whole room in, and at the railing holds a ring out over the edge and cannot let it go.
poems.thesis: Separation is a frame-rate: the body grieves at the world's speed and the soul at its own — and what returns from the split is not relief but accuracy: what isn't mine, I still can not give.
poems.tone: Restless bodily rhythm against the slower drift of the soul.

lines.text: The soul has escaped my body for the moment and left him on the dance floor. He can now just be
flesh and bones, rejection and heartache hit differently when there are no feelings afloat.
I want my soul now to imagine my body pulsing and head throbbing from the music and empty on
a crowded floor of sweated perfumes and temptations. Let's watch strangers collide and spark electric
currents that gamut the mood, a good one. We want him to be the last one to leave, prolonging the
bitter refraction inside the walls of an escape that few pleasures offer us. Now let us put my
soul in the middle of an open field at the equator of a planet much larger than my own
and much hotter. Cool me down by pouring unfiltered water out of the ice bath salted from the closest
moons from angels of the newest religions and its joys capturing my body transiting in a flash of
strobe lights. Their gracious cursor blessed me, only infinity will tell. Now bring my soul back
to my body to lean back, breathe in the smoke that now fills the room and tell myself how good
it is to finally get acquainted with the night, staring into unfamiliar yet relatable mountains
in the distance and wandering eyes and wandering thoughts within reach.

poems.title: YET, HEARD
poems.logline: Through a fawning crowd, past a moon that runs its phases over one walk, into a phone booth twice — mother's living room arriving as an inset with a tear down its crease, father's footprints lighting under his son's feet — while the break-up widens in the background of every shot, until the EX dissolves to weather and a motorcycle blinks its lamp at the man left standing.
poems.thesis: Farewell is not an event but a background process: it runs at its own rate behind every call, every walk, every prayer — and being heard does not stop it; it only means someone watched it happen with you.
poems.tone: Tender but unresolved; adjacent spaces hold grief without settling it.

lines.text: Accepting you'll never say nor ever feel, my love was real.
What isn't mine I still cannot give.
I gather my things to go.
Before I go, we look at the moon the way we used to see it
and settle down the stillnessism.
We talk for years and travel through time
and it feels so good.
We grow old together.
I believe maybe we could have it all,
or swing in my humbled late nights and heartbreaks
and an end story unchanging.
You help me gather my things to go.
Before I go, I call on my mother.
In tears, speaking of an abyss, she's never known.
And we talk for years and we closet wounds
and we explain my way of birth then and even after prayer.
What isn't mine I still cannot give.
We grow old together with the moon looking at us
the way we used to be.
As my tears fall between the creases and faith,
dancing on my own, maternal ears in tune.
She watches us gather my things to go.
Before I go, I call on my father.
Summon his calming demeanor from the yonders
and we walk for years and travel east toward the sunrises
and retrace his footsteps now and then.
Guiding a settling down moon the way it used to leave
and my tears fall between the creases
and wave shadows of the inner harbor.
We stroll, father and son, hearted and shaken.
Someone borrowed and someone blew.
Yet broken, yet hurt.

poems.title: MAGIC RIDE
poems.tagline: night replaced by morning, dot by dot
poems.logline: Not looking for a ride, he rubs his aggressions into the steel anyway — and one ride carries the whole film from black to white: through streets where heads twist twice, past loneliness shredded by his own noise, under a settling moon, across a grey hour where the frames themselves trade registers, into a believable morning that is chilly, and back to the shore where everything broke — arriving this time, not washing up.
poems.thesis: The magic still existing is not an event but a direction: darkness is crossed at riding speed, the stars you were given come inside, and the same shore means something different when you choose to stop there.
poems.tone: Independent, quietly amused and increasingly open; night gives way to morning.

lines.text: I wasn't looking for a ride, but here you are, blissful and oddly sensitive,
withering a soul purveying both the dark and the light worlds I've known.
So I rub my aggressions into your steel coverings and hop on to amuse myself.
Loneliness is having everything with no one to tell,
being everywhere with no one to love and escape,
wide-eyed and stone but alive and well, wandering with no clear end.
I let the noise block the noise so the way I ride through the streets with the swag and eyes turn,
has twists, improve, yeah, the magic still exists.
All preparations to live and dream in darkness I no longer desire.
The moon settles and the tease of distant stars subsides
and I can see a morning ahead for me.
It looks like a morning I could believe in,
a morning where loss and life aren't so well, ripe with sunlight that's deceptively warm.
The tripping of birds, feeling of nests, spring out of the night that has covered me,
with my own curiosities for a chance at an end, where everything will be okay.
I want to live in this feeling forever, blissful and oddly innocent,
riding in a way you can't help but double-click,
improve, yeah, the magic still exists.

poems.title: NEW DAY
poems.tagline: the temple assembles, one course at a time
poems.logline: The fog exhales its introduction over the ruin, and the ruin answers by lifting itself: stones float into a new base course, the broken arch straightens into a doorway, a parabolic shell draws itself left to right — and when the water arrives edgeless, the temple learns to reflect, the poet walks the waterline with his own inversion underfoot, and the sun ends up overhead.
poems.thesis: Catharsis is construction with the original materials: nothing new arrives — the same stones, the same arch, the same man — only the schedule runs the other way.
poems.tone: Calm reconstruction; masonry answers the earlier chapel damage.

lines.text: Even here is chilly in the morning.
River rafting fall covers the seas in the distance
and hugs the bases of tree-covered hills.
This world is at peace.
In silent resounds, choir chords calm the nerves of things I can't control
and offer them as keepsakes back to the higher powers.
Exhausted emotions carry forward a diminishing flame
to emit jazz tuned lyrics that heat and dry the morning dew.
All the remnants of the destruction revealed in the sunlight.
We can rebuild this temple.
It's a new day.
The catharsis evoked by loss in the painful crawl
along the cobblestone boulevards of broken dreams.
I can close a chapter and open a journal stored away
from moments of great clarity.
Words written from life's triumphs to offer a blueprint
of keeping faith alive and as majestic.
When words are read aloud and sung alone as gospels
to the lonely mirror's midnight hours,
the left tears drying with time that is common to past.
We can embrace a new day.
We can receive a new day.
We can welcome a new day.
Everything I've known and learned,
every circumference of life we're celebrating and believing
is here together in this sacred place,
reveling in the sunlight of a new beginning
with this world and a heart at peace.

poems.title: REUNION
poems.tagline: less time for words, more space for laughter
poems.logline: Decades later, inside the temple they rebuilt, three friends arrive through a door of light, trade their words in for laughter, go quiet for the crowned elders who stand faintly among them, flip the burning hourglass rather than let the occasion be one-time — and part ways trailing curls of wind, hearts still blinking in unison.
poems.thesis: Brotherhood is a shared clock: the hug synchronizes it, the laughter funds it, the flip extends it — and the winds can part ways without breaking the tempo.
poems.tone: Warm familiarity; individual gestures become shared laughter.

lines.text: Decades later, there was less time for words and more space for laughter, hugs with no reason,
loud voices so our hearts can be overheard. My mind drifts into the darkness of our afterlives,
and those rooms are empty. We are all here, each holding our glasses of burning sands
and known journeys, and grateful to every living tree in the forest for the shared years
and the shared memories. This is brotherhood. Smiles with no reason,
narrow differences so our hearts can be overheard. Decades later, we can place our ears upon the next
brother's soul and follow paths of hilltops and canyons, of blinding lights and infinite nights,
all too familiar and create the type of space for laughter
and football and recollections that bring us home every time.

poems.title: HOW TO WIN MY HEART
poems.logline: At the harbor cafe he watches couples orbit like Jupiter's moons and elders clutch what they kept, while his own love stories sit char-eaten at his elbow — so he harvests the flowers into his power instead, until a distant lit window says YOU'LL SEE ME, and instead of leaving toward anything, he sets the bouquet on the rail and sits back down: don't make me leave; I escaped here for a reason.
poems.thesis: Winning this heart is not pursuit but placement: stay where you escaped to, put the gathered power somewhere visible, and let the window keep its light on.
poems.tone: Watchful and guarded; attention gradually risks remaining with another person.

lines.text: I want you to notice me in a corner cafe
at the Harbor of the Heavens, wandering in thought,
discovering water on Jupiter's moons,
healing the sick with silent prayers
and molding a better world to return to
with every pulsing beat after walking alone.
I want you to really notice me
with the distances we couldn't avoid
and our younger selves watching and dreaming,
while our elders clutch their pearls,
hold their faith and breath closely,
freeing their worries peacefully.
I've journeyed beyond any place you can conceivably be.
So I thought, life has burned all of my love stories.
All ends led to losses,
victory-less seasons for a man that wanted just one win.
I could celebrate forever.
Ice has frozen in thought,
friendships in death and departure.
I've learned to love myself more,
manage loss and harvest a wizardry more brilliant
than the scarlet poppies and purple blossoms
at time and tears have just claimed.
Yet from a distant window, beautiful and calm,
hope tells me you'll see me.
And if you notice me and capture my eyes
as you refocus yours,
stepping back and letting them say hello,
all the fatigue of wandering alone in thought,
in windless seasons and scarlet poppies
won't prevent me from sharing a smile
worth the promise of my heart.

poems.title: HOT MINUTE
poems.tagline: everything learns to be weather, then a door
poems.logline: The haze gathers on the water and takes everything he built — boats, cafe, her window gently, the flowers last — then takes him ground-up until only the pulse blinks in the black. What follows is the suite remembering itself in twelve flashes, a dance of two entwined muses around one center, and an old vintage door opening on a slow warm party: the kind he once fell out of a window to escape, and now walks into, from the back, at his own speed, as the door closes and keeps him.
poems.thesis: Leaving and arriving are the same door seen from different registers: the suite opens with a fall out of a window and closes with a walk through a door — and the victory is not escaping the party, but choosing it.
poems.tone: Intense but accepting; built forms dissolve while remembered relations recur.

lines.text: Don't make me leave and go where promises, hearts,
spectrums of light-filled constellations are broken.
I escaped here for a reason,
believing this would give me a sharpened key of answers
in a more grounded bravado
for my life of conquests and queries.
The way you see things felt safe and timeless.
Whatever has terminated this moment, damn you,
but let it feel love and lost as we must endure,
absent artificial escapes and machine learning strengths
for my highs and lows as resource materials.
Well, I can't leave behind the impulse
that comes from battle scars
and can't leave behind the wisdom that brushes gray tones
into our melanin after disappointments and defeats.
I trust that you'll be fine.
I escaped here for a reason.
Our dance together is a victory to entwine muses,
immersed in twisted dons for a hot minute,
and a genesis of a New Testament as it ends.
